instagram.caption:
A triangle cuts a square hole — patented 1914.

The bit is a Reuleaux triangle. Measure it any direction: the width never changes. That constant width is what lets it trace a square path inside a floating chuck.

Check your pocket. UK 20p and 50p coins are the same shape family — Reuleaux heptagons, seven curved sides, still round enough to roll in any slot.

Save this and check your pocket.

alt_text: White card with the title 'The drill that cuts squares.' at the top, Axi the mascot reading in the upper corner. Three photographs follow in sequence: a drill press cutting a square hole into a brass plate under a warm lamp; a Reuleaux-triangle drill bit resting in caliper jaws showing equal widths on every side; and two heptagonal UK coins — a 50p and a 20p — on a dark oak table. Between the second and third images, formula lines build from a single arc length up to P = πw.
